title: Enhanced Endosome Formation of Lipid-Modified DNA via Cell Membranes
content: We have developed nucleic acid-based micelles (DNA micelles) as drug delivery systems and observed that the amphiphilic lipid-modified DNA constituting the DNA micelles induces cellular uptake. In previous studies using lipid-DNA-based nanoparticles for delivering nucleic acid agents, such as immune adjuvants, antigens, and siRNAs, we confirmed that effective cellular delivery was achievable without the assistance of transfection reagents [1, 2]. Moreover, several studies have reported that membrane deformation induced by extracellular materials leads to internalization [3, 4]. Based on this, we hypothesize that inserting lipid-DNA into the cell membrane can induce membrane deformation, leading to cellular internalization. Thus, this study aims to demonstrate the role of interactions between lipid-DNA and the cell membrane in inducing endocytosis-like internalization and identify the internalization pathway of DNA micelles using different analytical models.
